newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Iraqi convicts suffer mass poisoning in Cyprus.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi convicts suffer mass poisoning in Cyprus.

text.p: Nineteen Iraqi convicts in Cyprus were rushed to hospital on Friday after poisoning themselves with toilet detergents, prison and hospital officials said.
The Iraqis, jailed for illegal entry, consider themselves political refugees and want residence permits to stay on the island, prison director George Anastassiades told Reuters.
"They are trying to blackmail the state into releasing them and giving them permission to remain in Cyprus but it will not work," Anastassiades said.
He said the Iraqis apparently consumed disinfectant and toilet cleaner, easily accessible in the washrooms of their wing at the central prisons in the capital Nicosia.

The nineteen, who were admitted to hospital for observation with vomiting and abdominal pains, are part of a group of 34 Iraqis jailed for eight months for entering the island illegally. They have completed four months of their sentence.

It is the second incident in the space of a week. On Christmas Eve three Iraqis jumped off the prison chapel while another was left swinging on a tree for several hours, demanding permission to remain in Cyprus. The three sustained minor injuries while the fourth was coaxed down by prison officials.
Foreigners jailed for illegal entry are deported once their sentences are completed.
Anastassiades said the authorities were in contact with the United Nations regugee agency UNHCR in an attempt to find a solution.
